column1: # WALL LEDGER — one line per recorded wall. TAB-separated, 7 fields:
#   id  polarity  scope  anchor  reopen  date  claim
# polarity  MISSING  the wall says a CAPABILITY is absent.  0 anchor hits -> the wall
#                    STANDS (nobody has built the prerequisite). >0 -> it landed.
#           DEFECT   the wall says a DEFECT is present.  0 anchor hits -> the defect is
#                    GONE, so the wall is retired. >0 -> the defect is still live.
#           RUN      the wall is a NUMBER or a BUILD, so its prerequisite is a re-run,
#                    not a grep. Reported OUT-OF-SCOPE, never guessed at with a pattern.
# scope     ONE path relative to the repo root. The grep runs on THAT FILE ONLY, in the
#           working copy AND at `git show HEAD:<path>`, and a scope that is readable in
#           NEITHER is `NO-SCOPE` -- a refusal, because a grep of nothing answers nothing.
# anchor    an -E pattern. A line whose first non-blank character is `#` is dropped, so a
#           name quoted in a COMMENT cannot satisfy an anchor. `nvdev.bend:66` is the proof.
# reopen    the check whose result would clear the wall.
# date      YYYY-MM-DD of the measurement that PRODUCED the wall, not the date it was read.
# claim     the wall as recorded, verbatim enough to grep for in the tree.
# POLARITY IS NOT COSMETIC. An anchor written to match the DEFECT under a MISSING reading
# inverts the verdict. Three of the first nine rows were inverted that way and all three
# read "ABSENT, the wall stands" for capabilities that had already landed.
# The independent hand-measured truth for each row is `walls.truth.tsv`. That file is NOT
# produced by wallcheck.py; it is the denominator the error rate is computed against.
